messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty -> ENG-ONCALL: firing alert 'serving-router:5xx-rate-spike' (P2). 3 pages sent. Affected service: serving-router (us-west). Link: https://pagerduty.example/alerts/PD123456 :rotating_light:

alex: acked. oncall here. pinging infra, will grab logs. :eyes:

maria: ack from me too, standing by. seeing a cascade of 502/503 from router -> backend-pop.

ben: i'm on the infra side, pulling metrics. initial look shows burst of 5xx starting 30s ago, CPU on router pods spiked, but replicas seem healthy. possible brief KV-cache miss storm.

samir: checking downstream model-pool health, a few GPUs OOM'd recently but restarted. not sure if related. any customer visible errors?

alex: customer-facing dashboards show a small bump in error-rate for long-seq requests ( > 2k tokens). top traces show timeouts between router -> model-proxy around 500-700ms then 504.

maria: can we temporarily route traffic away from us-west to us-east for non-low-latency routes? we can favor dedicated capacity there.

ben: try a local mitigation first: bump router replicas + increase request timeout to 90s for the gateway to avoid early 504s while we stabilize. I'll run scaling now.

ben: (run) kubectl scale deploy/serving-router -n prod --replicas=8 && kubectl patch deploy/serving-router -n prod --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/env/0/value","value":"90"}]'

alex: applied scale, replicas going 4 -> 8. timeout patch applied. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: PagerDuty: Alert 'serving-router:5xx-rate-spike' acknowledged by alex. Escalation paused.

samir: watching logs, KV-cache miss rate spiked x12, many warmup hits concurrently. likely load-pattern: many cold-start long prompts hitting different contexts.

maria: can we enable prefix caching for high-volume customers temporarily? if not, let's apply a 10s rate limit per token for new sessions to dampen warmup.

ben: quick throttle rule added to gateway for new sessions: 50 rps per client-id. implementing a soft-shed at edge for ephemeral sessions.

alex: alert noise down but still intermittent 5xx for a handful of requests. customer impact so far: transient failed inference for ~0.8% of requests in us-west 2xx -> 5xx. Not widespread.

samir: model-pool OOMs were unrelated — older driver bug restarted a few nodes. cleared. not seeing continuing OOM.

maria: PD sent auto-resolve? I see: PagerDuty: 'serving-router:5xx-rate-spike' auto-resolved (no active incidents).

alex: confirming logs show error-rate back to baseline after scale + throttle. Looks like a transient warmup+burst pattern. No customer escalations in support queue yet.

ben: i'll leave the temporary scaling and throttle in place for 15 minutes, then roll back if stable. adding a 30m follow-up ticket to eng-runtime to investigate warmup storms.

oncall-bot: Handoff reminder -> next oncall is samir in 45m. please add summary to the incident tracker.

alex: quick summary for tracker: transient 5xx spike in us-west due to KV-cache warmup + concurrent long-seq requests causing router timeouts. Mitigations: scaled router 4->8, patched gateway timeout to 90s, added soft throttle for new sessions. Auto-resolved by PD after stabilization. Follow-ups: persistent warmup mitigations, better pre-warming for long prompts, investigate driver OOM bug.

maria: adding support note: low customer impact (~0.8% requests, brief window). monitoring for 1hr.

samir: ack received. will pick up follow-up ticket. handing off observability to oncoming shift.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: Incident closed by auto-resolve. If errors re-appear, new page will be opened. :white_check_mark:
